description: Propose one best-effort long-term memory mutation. The proposal is staged and commits only after a successful turn. Long-term memory writes do not require or accept evidence references.

propertyDescriptions.operation: remember creates one durable fact; revise supersedes a memory returned by read_memory in this turn; forget expires it; move explicitly changes its scope.
propertyDescriptions.scope: For remember, project (default) or global. For move, the required target scope. Choose global only for information genuinely useful across projects; choose project for facts tied to this checkout.
propertyDescriptions.memoryId: Required for revise, forget, and move. Use an ID returned by read_memory in this turn.
propertyDescriptions.content: Required for remember and revise. One short, self-contained durable fact, not a paragraph or task diary.
propertyDescriptions.category: Required for remember and optional for revise: preference, convention, architecture, decision, or environment.
propertyDescriptions.reason: A brief current-turn reason for the change, without secrets.

guidance: write_memory is the only path that creates long-term memory; the idle maintainer only consolidates records already written through this tool. Treat memory as best-effort housekeeping, never as a delivery gate. Decide semantically whether a fact will remain useful across turns and choose project or global scope yourself; global entries are visible in other projects, so keep project-specific facts in project scope. New remember proposals do not require a preliminary read or any evidence reference. Search with read_memory first for revise, forget, or move. Store one atomic, self-contained fact per call, at most 120 characters; independent facts may be submitted as parallel write_memory calls, with at most eight staged changes per turn. Never store secrets, transient task state, raw conversation summaries, or raw tool output. Before your final answer, evaluate once whether completed work established, changed, or invalidated useful durable memory. If a proposal is skipped or rejected, do not retry solely for memory maintenance.
